papers.title_en: Realistic Counterfactual Explanations via Denial Constraints
papers.authors: Avia Asael, Nave Frost, Amir Gilad, Daniel Deutch
papers.evidence: 运用拒绝约束生成现实可行的反事实解释，将符号约束与机器学习可解释性结合
papers.tldr: 反事实解释是解释AI预测的一种方式，但现有方法追求距离小和多样性，常生成不真实的实例。本文引入数据管理中的拒绝约束来刻画现实性，并结合数据清洗技术将不真实的反事实转换为符合约束的版本。实验表明该方法在保持距离和多样性的同时显著提升真实性，且优化加速有效。
papers.abstract_en: In the realm of Explainable AI, classification results are often explained via counterfactuals (CFs for short), which are (ideally small) perturbations to an instance that lead to a change of classification label. Such CFs may serve as explanations for the prediction, pinpointing the features that were important. Existing explainability solutions typically aim at minimizing the distance of CFs from the original instance so that they are specific to it, and/or maximizing the diversity of CFs to cover multiple facets of the reasons underlying the prediction. In this paper, we note that in pursuing these aims, state-of-the-art explainability solutions may (and often do) yield counterfactual explanations that do not correspond to realistic instances. This limits their applicability and usefulness in practice. To remedy this, we combine ideas from Explainable AI with ideas from data management. Specifically, we capture realism of CFs via logical constraints that hold with respect to a dataset of examples (e.g., training set); the class of such constraints that we focus on is that of denial constraints, extensively studied in the context of relational databases. Algorithmically, we then combine explainable AI solutions to yield CFs, with ideas from data cleaning that we adapt to this unique setting, to transform CFs into realistic ones. Extensive experiments across four datasets validate that our solutions achieve realism with relatively minor compromise in terms of distance and diversity. They further validate that the dedicated optimizations that we have developed to speed up the search for CFs are indeed highly effective.

papers.title_en: Decoupled Physical Modeling and Execution for Physics Reasoning
papers.authors: Ye Zhang, Xuehang Guo, Rui Pan, Pengfei Yu, Denghui Zhang, Manling Li, Qingyun Wang
papers.evidence: 面向物理推理的大模型结构化建模
papers.tldr: 物理推理要求先构建一致的物理模型，再进行数学计算，但现有大规模语言模型往往把建模与计算混在一起，导致处理物理问题时表现不佳。受人类先建立表示后计算的方式启发，本文提出一个统一框架：将显式编码物理建模过程的中间表示蒸馏出来，并采用两阶段后训练策略——先用监督微调建立结构化建模，再用基于评分标准的强化学习提升建模质量。在PhysReason、PhyX、SeePhys等多个多模态物理基准上，该方法相比GRPO平均提升约3%，说明显式物理建模是改进小型视觉语言模型物理推理能力的有效策略。
papers.abstract_en: Physics reasoning requires constructing a consistent model of the underlying physical system rather than relying solely on symbolic or formula-based manipulation. Although large language models have shown strong ability in solving math and coding problems, they still struggle with physics problems, as these problems entangle the physical modeling process with mathematical calculations. Humans approach physics by first building a representation of the system before performing calculations. Inspired by this, we introduce a unified framework that distills intermediate representations that explicitly encode the physical modeling process and adopt a two-stage post-training strategy, where supervised fine-tuning establishes structured modeling, and reinforcement learning with rubric-based feedback improves the quality of the modeling process. Experiments on multiple multimodal physics benchmarks show that our approach generally improves physical reasoning performance across different models and datasets. Across PhysReason, PhyX, and SeePhys, physical modeling outperforms GRPO by ~3% on average. showing that explicit physical modeling is an effective strategy for improving physics reasoning in small VLMs.
